# Homeward at Dusk

The last gold leaves are loosening from the trees,
And dusk folds blue along the quiet lane.
I carry twilight softly on my sleeves,
While chimney smoke unthreads into the rain.
The porch light blooms, a small and faithful star,
The gate remembers how my fingers turn.
Beyond the glass, familiar shadows are,
And in the hearth, old embers wake and burn.
My footsteps find the stones they knew before,
A kettle hums; the hallway holds its breath.
I cross the threshold, leave the road outdoors,
And home gathers me gently from the dusk.

=== file-001.md ===
The Way Back

The road gathers dusk beneath my feet,
Leaves whisper gold along the lane,
A chimney lifts its ribboned heat,
And windows bloom against the rain.
I carry daylight in my coat,
The west has dimmed to copper fire,
A sparrow folds its final note,
While porch lights kindle one by one.
At last, the gate knows me by sound,
The door gives way, the kettle sings,
And all the wandering miles fall down
Into the warmth that homeward brings.

=== file-001.md ===
The Warm Window

I turn where the last gold leaves cross the lane,
The evening gathers blue along the eaves.
A kettle's small promise waits beyond the pane,
While dusk moves softly through the thinning trees.
My footsteps find the stones they knew before,
Past fences brushed with copper, russet light.
The old gate gives its familiar, gentle roar,
And one porch lamp keeps watch against the night.
I lift the latch; the quiet lets me in.
The house breathes warmth around my travel-worn coat.
Somewhere, a clock begins its patient hymn,
And home, like a hearth, rises in my throat.

=== file-001.md ===
Coming Home in Autumn

Twilight gathers copper in the lane,
The last leaves turn like sparks along the wall.
I follow dusk through fields of fading rain,
While swallows stitch the quiet sky and fall.
A window blooms, one amber star ahead,
The gate remembers softly as I near.
The kettle hums its welcome, warmly fed,
And old floorboards wake to say I’m here.
I set my coat beside the evening fire,
The woods breathe silver under darkening eaves.
Home holds the day, then lifts my heart still higher,
While autumn settles gently on the leaves.

=== file-001.md ===
The Last Turn Home

Evening gathers copper in the trees,
And smoke-blue shadows lengthen by the lane.
I follow homeward, listening to the breeze,
That sifts the dry leaves softly like rain.
The porch light blooms before I reach the gate,
A small, warm star against the cooling sky.
The kettle waits; the windows hold their glow,
While swallows stitch the dimness as they fly.
My footsteps know the stones beneath my feet,
The key turns once, and all the miles release.
Inside, the ordinary world is sweet:
A coat, a cup, a room, and quiet peace.

# Returning Home

The autumn evening folds its amber light,
I turn along the lane beneath the trees.
Dry leaves go skittering in small delight,
And chimney smoke drifts softly on the breeze.
A porch lamp blooms beyond the garden wall,
The windows hold a warmth I know by heart.
My footsteps slow; the day grows quiet all,
While red leaves loosen, flutter, and depart.
I hear the kettle murmur through the door,
A familiar coat hangs waiting in the hall.
I leave the fading gold across the floor,
And step inside where evening gathers all.

# Returning Home

The evening settles softly on the lane,
And amber leaves go spinning through the air;
I hear the old gate creak beside the rain,
While smoke from distant chimneys curls somewhere.
My footsteps follow paths I used to know,
Past hedges darkening beneath the sky;
The first cool stars appear, row after row,
And swallows gather low before they fly.
A window glows beyond the garden wall,
A kettle hums, a chair waits near the flame;
I lift the latch and hear the hallway call,
Then set my coat aside and speak my name.

# Returning Home

The evening settles over the street,
and leaves move along the curb.
I walk home with my hands in my pockets,
listening to the cars go by.
The air smells faintly of wood smoke,
and the sky is turning gray.
A porch light comes on down the block,
while someone closes a gate.
I see my windows through the trees,
warm against the cooling air.
I reach the door before it gets dark,
and step inside for the night.

The Walk Home

The evening cools along the quiet street.
Dry leaves turn beneath my waiting feet.
The shops pull down their signs and close.
A chimney sends up threads of smoke.
I pass the park, now dim and brown.
The last bus sighs and settles down.
A porch light warms the path ahead.
I think of soup and books and bed.
The key is cool inside my hand.
I hear the floorboards where I stand.
Behind me, daylight leaves the sky.
I shut the door and settle in.

# Home at Dusk

The bus lets me off by the old corner store.
Dry leaves turn slowly along the curb.
The windows gather the last amber light.
A cool wind follows me up the street.
I carry bread and apples in a paper bag.
The houses grow quiet behind their trees.
Somewhere, a kettle begins to sing.
Smoke lifts softly from a chimney nearby.
I find our porch beneath the darkening sky.
The key turns warm against my waiting hand.
Inside, the hallway holds the scent of wood.
I step through the door, and evening comes home.

# Autumn Homecoming

The evening folds its amber light,
And leaves drift softly through the lane.
I hear the old gate breathe at night,
Then footsteps fade beneath the rain.
Warm windows gather dusk inside,
A kettle sings behind the door.
I set my wandering coat aside,
And feel the floor beneath me once more.
The chimney lifts a thread of gray,
While crickets hush the cooling air.
I whisper home, and end the day,
With autumn glowing everywhere.

The evening folds its amber light,
And leaves come whispering down;
I walk the road through cooling air,
Past fields turned bronze and brown.

A kettle hums behind our door,
